sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident that occurred on 08.10.2023.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 08.10.2023 at about 7.30 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding on the motor cycle bearing No. KA-05-LJ- 0713 on Thamaiah road, Padmanabhanagar, Banashankari 2nd stage, Bangalore and when he reached near Ayyanger Bakery, at that time the driver of the car bearing No. KA-03-MC-0427 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner came on wrong lane and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Maharaja Agrasen Hospital,
Bengaluru wherein he was admitted as inpatient and he has spent Rs.2,00,000/-
towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as delivery boy and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 & 3 are the policy holder and RC owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.

3. After service of notices, respondent No.2 & 3- policy holder and owner remained absent hence,
placed exparte.

Respondent No.1 - insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the car bearing No. KA-03-MC-0427 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to proof of the policy.
Further contended that, non-compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
This respondent has specifically denies the occurrence, mode of the accident and also involvement of car bearing No. KA-03-MC-0427.
The respondent No.1 contended that the driver of the car was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Further denied the age, avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.1 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:

Also examined two witnesses as PW.2 & 3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.19 to Ex.P.22.
The first respondent insurance company has not adduced any rebuttal evidence.

The Ex.P2 statement was given in the hospital on 9.10.2023 at about 2.30 p.m. by alleging the rash and negligent driving and accident by the driver of car bearing No. KA-03-MC-0427 at about 7.30 p.m. of 8.10.2023.
In this regard, if we see the Ex.8 wound certificate, Ex.P11- discharge summary it evidentiates that the petitioner admitted to Maharaja Agrasen Hospital on 8.10.2023 at about 7.40 p.m.

Thus, it is very prudent that as the accident was in the night 7.30 p.m. the petitioner imemdiately admitted to the Karan Kumar M vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125913067/

10. The contents of Ex.P2 & 1 is in consonance with the contents of petition about the rash and negligence driving by the driver of car bearing No. KA03- MC-427.
Ex.P3 is mahazar and Ex.P.4 rough sketch drawn by the police at the time of investigation.

On perusal of the contents of Ex.P3 spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 rough sketch appended therein, the accident spot is in the left side portion of the road in whcih the petitioner was proceeding and the driver of car bearing No.
KA-03-MC-0427 who came from opposite side by changing his lane came to the wrong side i.e., his right side portion of the road and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner.
As per the spot mahazar the driver of car bearing No. KA03-MC-427 came to his right portion of the road instead of proceeding in left side portion of the road and caused the accident.

The Ex.P7 is the IMV report,
wherein the right hand side bumper and front side axel of the car bearing No. KA03-MC-427 has got damaged and front portion of the motor cycle of the petitioner has also got damaged.

The contents of Ex.P3 & 4 spot mahazar and rough sketch along with contents of Ex.P7- IMV report, establishes the negligence of the driver of car bearing No. KA03-MC-427.
11.
The respondent No.1-insurance company even after sufficient opportunity has not lead any evidence by leading the rebuttal evidence in support of their defence.
The respondent No.2 & 3 being the policy holders and owner of the offending vehicle remained exparte and has not denied the alleged negligence.
12. The Ex.P8 is wound certificate and Ex.P10 & 11 being the discharge summary wherein supported the case of the petitioner.
The contents of Ex.P8 and Ex.P10
corroborates with the contents of complaint.
Ex.P9 charge sheet is filed against the driver of car bearing No. KA-03-MC-427 for the offence punishable under Sec. 279 & 338 of IPC.

By producing these documents, the petitioner prima-facie established the occurrence of accident and also the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending car bearing No.KA-03-MC-0427.
13.

Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 on oath supported by Ex.P-9 which is the charge sheet and the documents annexed therewith, this court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to rash and actionable negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing No. KA-03-MC-0427.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the inc ident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case at hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing No. KA- 03-MC-0427 resulting in petitioner sustaining injuries.
During the course of cross examination of petitioner, except a suggestion nothing has been elicited so as to disprove the case of the petitioner.
There are no material evidence to prove that the petitioner's negligence was the reason for the said accident.
15. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 8.10.2023 which is caused by the driver of the car bearing No.KA-03-MC-0427.
There is no reasons to discard the evidence of petitioner.

ISSUE NO.2:
16.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by respondent No.3.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.

The petitioner examined In-charger at Mahaveera Agrasena Hospital as PW.2, through him got marked Ex.P19 & 20.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 24 years.
The Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P15 shows that the petitioner was aged about 24 years at the time of accident.

As per the discharge summaries marked at Ex.P10 & 11 petitioner was admitted to Maharaja Agrasen Hospital for two times i.e.
on 8.10.2023 and discharged on 12.10.2023 and again admitted on 24.1.2024 and discharged on the same day it shows that he sustained fracture shaft of left femur with tibial spine avulsion injury.
The two times admission was done by the petitioner for initial operation on 9.10.2023 and also an another operation for delayed union.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.80,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced advance receipts as per Ex.P13 and medical bills as per Ex.P14, amounting to Rs.1,22,874/-.
These bills are not disputed by the respondent and no grounds are made out to disbelieve this bill.
These bills are supported with Ex.P10 & 11 discharge summaries, Ex.P12 medical prescriptions and also Ex.P20- inpatient case details.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitle by rounding off the same i.e., Rs.1,23,000/- under this head.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was working as delivery boy and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any document.
In the absence of any document the notional income of the petitioner is considered in the year 2023 at Rs.16,000/- p.m.
As per the discharge summaries marked at Ex.P10 & 11- the petitioner was admitted to Maharaja Agrasen Hospital totally for 6 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total four months period including 6 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.

So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,000 X 4 months =
Rs.64,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner examined Dr. S.A.
Somashekar, working as Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital as PW.3, through him clinical notes and X-ray are marked at Ex.P.21 & P.22.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained fracture of left femur with tibial spine avulsion injury.

He examined the Karan Kumar M vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125913067/
6 petitioner for assessment of disability.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Petitioner suffered total disability of 38% to the left lower limb and 19% to the whole body disability.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
Further PW.3 has also stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants, which may costs Rs.40,000/-.
According to the petitioner he was working as delivery boy and suffered with fracture of left femur with tibial spine avulsion injury.
As per the evidence of PW.3 doctor and recent clinical examination and X-ray as per Ex.P21 & 22, out of the two fractures one fracture is united and another fracture is partially united.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his occupation to some extent.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 17% to the whole body.
The petitioner has produced his Aadhar card which is marked at Ex.P15, as per this document the year of birth of the petitioner is shown as 1999.
The accident was occurred in the year-2023.
So, as on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 24 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '18'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 18 X 17% =Rs. 5,87,520/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P10 & 11 discharge summaries, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 6 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P6 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of injuries and the period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.45,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 6 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the injuries as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.6,000/- in total.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.60,000/- under this head.
h) Towards future medical expenses:
PW.3 stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants which may cost around Rs.40,000/-.
By looking to the nature of injuries sustained the treatment taken, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:

Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 & 3 are the policy holder and RC owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the car bearing No. KA-03-MC-0427.
No other grounds are made out by the respondent No.1 insurance company to consider the contributory negligence by the petitioner or violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.2 & 3.

Hence, the respondent No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.1 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1 & 2.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. except on the amount awarded under the head of future medical expenses.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
18.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total  compensation amount of Rs.9,95,520/-
(Rupees Nine lakhs ninety five thousand five hundred twenty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. (excluding future medical expenses), from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
Further it is clarified that the amount awarded under the head of future medical expenses shall not carries any interest.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
